lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: responsibilities that begin at majority

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic responsibilities that begin at majority task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Given a provided generic list of responsibility-type examples that begin at the age of majority (such as 'may be able to sign certain contracts' or 'certain protections change'), the learner sorts each into 'verify locally, this varies by place' versus 'broadly true in most places,' explicitly modeling skepticism toward any single source, including this lesson's own materials.
safetyNotes: This lesson does not assert which specific responsibilities apply in the learner's actual location — the sorting skill is the point, not memorizing a fixed answer key.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l03-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l03-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l03-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l03-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: This lesson itself makes claims about what generally happens at majority. What would you want to check before fully trusting even this material?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g12-u04-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Discriminating judgment: Items are sorted into both categories with plausible reasoning. | Healthy skepticism: The final reflection names something worth checking even about this lesson's own claims. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner write one additional responsibility-type example of their own and sort it, explaining their reasoning.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic responsibilities that begin at majority task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: responsibilities that begin at majority worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Given a provided generic list of responsibility-type examples that begin at the age of majority (such as 'may be able to sign certain contracts' or 'certain protections change'), the learner sorts each into 'verify locally, this varies by place' versus 'broadly true in most places,' explicitly modeling skepticism toward any single source, including this lesson's own materials.

Model move 2: Before sorting, name one 'fact' you've heard about turning 18 that you're not actually sure is true everywhere.
Model move 3: Sort the provided list into 'verify locally' versus 'broadly true in most places.'

Model check: Discriminating judgment: Items are sorted into both categories with plausible reasoning. | Healthy skepticism: The final reflection names something worth checking even about this lesson's own claims.

resources.title: responsibilities that begin at majority action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for responsibilities that begin at majority.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: responsibilities that begin at majority coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Given a provided generic list of responsibility-type examples that begin at the age of majority (such as 'may be able to sign certain contracts' or 'certain protections change'), the learner sorts each into 'verify locally, this varies by place' versus 'broadly true in most places,' explicitly modeling skepticism toward any single source, including this lesson's own materials.
Coach direction: Before sorting, name one 'fact' you've heard about turning 18 that you're not actually sure is true everywhere.
Learner prompt: Have you ever heard a claim about what changes at 18 that you suspect might not be true everywhere? What was it?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: responsibilities that begin at majority complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Sort the provided list into 'verify locally' versus 'broadly true in most places.'
Response 1 (t2-p1): I sorted every item on the provided list into one of the two categories.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I did not leave any item unsorted or mark any item as 'definitely true everywhere' without qualification.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: responsibilities that begin at majority minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: This lesson itself makes claims about what generally happens at majority. What would you want to check before fully trusting even this material?

Success checks: Discriminating judgment: Items are sorted into both categories with plausible reasoning. | Healthy skepticism: The final reflection names something worth checking even about this lesson's own claims.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: responsibilities that begin at majority supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g12-u04-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional responsibilities that begin at majority condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Discriminating judgment: Items are sorted into both categories with plausible reasoning. | Healthy skepticism: The final reflection names something worth checking even about this lesson's own claims..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
